First-party behaviour tests of scenes saved with geometry by key and of the canvas font's options; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party font for 3D text traced from the page's own fonts: characters drawn on a canvas, their pixel edges linked into loops and simplified; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0. Edge tracing and Ramer-Douglas-Peucker simplification are standard techniques; no third-party source.

First-party behaviour tests of bounds that follow geometry moved in place, distance culling, the sky share of the atmosphere fog and sky colours given as fractions; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party behaviour tests of navigation laid over a height field, agents that turn toward the way they walk, and the centre and distance of streamed terrain tiles; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party behaviour tests of a positional sound whose rate changes the voices playing, and of buffers made from samples, on a small stand-in for Web Audio; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party distance-field modelling: rounded primitives, smooth union, subtraction and intersection, mirroring and displacement, meshed by surface nets with field normals, blended vertex colours and baked occlusion; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0. The primitive distance functions and the polynomial smooth minimum are the standard published closed forms; surface nets is a standard technique; no third-party source.

First-party mesh simplification by edge collapse under the quadric error metric (Garland and Heckbert, 1997), extended to vertex colours (Garland and Heckbert, 1998), keeping open edges, attributes and material groups; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0. No third-party source.
First-party behaviour tests of distance-field shapes, the meshes made from them and the simplifier; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party binary glTF 2.0 writer for geometry, vertex colours, material groups, node transforms and material factors, written from the public glTF 2.0 specification; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0. No third-party source.

First-party tool that draws a model made in code from four sides in a headless browser and reports its numbers, so the person or agent who made it can look at it; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party behaviour tests of turned and extruded shapes, patterns, worn edges, colour-aware simplification, .glb export and the World3D import map; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party rigging of distance-field models: bones at joints, skin weights from the distance to the parts each bone moves, and clips from poses of named bones; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0. No third-party source.
First-party behaviour tests of rigs of distance-field models: bones, weights, skinning by bone and clips; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.
First-party levels of detail for distance-field models, each simplified from the one before; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.
First-party tool that makes models written in code ahead of time and writes each as a .glb; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.
First-party behaviour tests of sharp hard surfaces, levels of detail, baked models and the notes of the model preview; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.

First-party procedural surfaces (wood, stone, brick, plaster, metal, cloth, bark) drawn by fragment and normal hooks in GLSL and WGSL from value noise projected in world space; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0. Value noise and fractal sums are standard techniques; no third-party source.
First-party tests of the surface materials' sources in both shading languages and of their parameters; independently authored with AI assistance; Apache-2.0.
